title: B2 · L13 — Reduced relative clauses
topic: Shortening relative clauses by omitting who/which + be
description: Cómo acortar cláusulas relativas omitiendo 'who/which/that + be' para lograr un estilo más conciso.

questions.prompt: Situación: reescribes una descripción para hacerla más ligera.
questions.question: Reduce: 'The book which is lying on the table is mine.'
options: The book lying on the table is mine.
The book laid on the table is mine.
The book to lie on the table is mine.
The book lies on the table is mine.
questions.explanation: Cuando la relativa tiene 'BE + -ing', se omiten 'which/who + be' y queda solo el participio -ing: 'which is lying' → 'lying'. Reduce el 'ruido gramatical' y aporta fluidez. La opción B ('laid') es agramatical aquí porque 'lay/laid' es verbo transitivo distinto de 'lie/lying'.
examples: The girl sitting next to me at the wedding turned out to be my cousin. → conversación casual
The car parked outside our building blocking the entrance is his.

questions.prompt: Simplificas una frase para el pie de foto de una revista.
questions.question: Reduce: 'The house that was built in 1900 needs repairs.'
options: The house building in 1900 needs repairs.
The house built in 1900 needs repairs.
The house to build in 1900 needs repairs.
The house was built in 1900 needs repairs.
questions.explanation: Con la voz pasiva ('was built'), se omiten 'that + was' y queda sólo el participio pasado: 'built in 1900'. Regla clave: -ing para acción activa/continua; PP para pasiva o estado. La opción D es agramatical porque genera dos verbos sin conector.
examples: The letter written entirely by hand felt somehow more personal. → detalle sentimental
The bridge destroyed during the war has finally been rebuilt after 30 years.

questions.statement: Las cláusulas relativas reducidas siempre omiten tanto el pronombre relativo como el verbo 'be'.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. La reducción SÓLO es posible cuando la relativa contiene el patrón 'who/which/that + be + -ing/PP'. Se omiten los dos elementos (pronombre + be) simultáneamente. Si no hay 'be', no se puede reducir con este método — habría que reformular la oración de otra forma.
examples: Full: The man who is standing there is my mentor.
Reduced: The man standing there is my mentor. → misma información, estilo más ligero

questions.text: The candidates selected for the second interview will be contacted by email.
questions.explanation: Reducción típica de comunicaciones de RRHH y procesos de selección. 'Selected for the second interview' = 'who are selected'. Prosodia formal y neutra. Connected speech: 'selected for' se enlaza suave, y 'contacted by email' fluye con la /d/ suavizada. 'By email' (nunca 'by the email' — sin artículo).
examples: Anyone interested in the internal position should apply through the portal by Friday.
Students enrolled in the online course will receive their materials by end of day.

questions.prompt: Describes a los invitados de una fiesta corporativa.
questions.question: Which sentence uses a reduced clause correctly?
options: The people invited to the party were all my colleagues.
The people who invited to the party were my colleagues.
The people inviting to the party were my colleagues.
The people they invited to the party were my colleagues.
questions.explanation: 'Invited' es participio pasado con sentido pasivo (fueron invitados). 'The people who were invited' se reduce a 'the people invited'. La opción C ('inviting') implicaría que ellos hacían la invitación — cambio de significado por confundir activo/pasivo.
examples: The students chosen for the exchange programme are truly exceptional. → tono profesor orgulloso
The letters sent yesterday afternoon should reach clients by tomorrow morning.

questions.statement: 'The man who works here' se puede reducir a 'The man working here'.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'Who works' (presente simple, acción habitual) se convierte en '-ing' cuando reducimos la relativa. Aunque en la forma completa no aparece 'be', el sentido continuo/habitual permite la reducción a participio activo. Es un uso muy natural y común, especialmente en descripciones.
examples: The people living next door are incredibly friendly — always inviting us over.
Anyone speaking English should raise their hand for the next activity.

questions.prompt: Empareja cada sujeto con su cláusula relativa reducida:

pairs.right: sitting on the bench is my sister.
written by García Márquez won a prize.
interested in the position should apply.

questions.explanation: Todos son ejemplos de reducción. -ing para acción activa/continua (sitting, working); participio pasado para pasiva o estado (written, renovated, interested). La distinción activo/pasivo es la única regla que hay que dominar para no confundirse.
examples: The books lying on the desk are all mine — please don't move them.
The cakes made by my grandmother following her secret recipe are legendary.

questions.prompt: Identifica qué relativa NO admite reducción.
questions.question: Which relative clause CANNOT be reduced?
options: The car which is parked outside is mine.
The car which I bought last week is mine.
The girl who is talking is my friend.
The book which was written in 1900 is famous.
questions.explanation: Sólo se pueden reducir relativas con 'BE + -ing' o 'BE + PP'. 'Which I bought' no contiene 'be' — el verbo es 'bought' (past simple activo), sin auxiliar. No hay nada que 'quitar' con este método. Para acortar habría que suprimir sólo el pronombre: 'The car I bought last week is mine' (sin 'which').
examples: Cannot reduce with -ing/PP: The book (which) I read last month — sin 'be'.
Can reduce: The book (which was) read at the ceremony — con 'be'.

questions.target: The applications received before the deadline will be reviewed by the committee next week.
questions.explanation: Reducción con participio pasado en registro profesional/corporativo (RRHH, becas, licitaciones). Prosodia formal, ritmo pausado. Connected speech: 'received before' se enlaza con /d/ suave. Nativos en emails formales añaden 'kindly note that...' o 'please be advised that...' antes de estas frases para reforzar la formalidad.
examples: The proposals submitted online will be considered on a rolling basis until the position is filled.
The papers signed today at the meeting will be filed with legal by tomorrow morning.

questions.prompt: Un anuncio en el tablón de la oficina.
questions.question: Reduce: 'Anyone who is interested in joining should sign up.'
options: Anyone to interest in joining should sign up.
Anyone interested in joining should sign up.
Anyone interesting in joining should sign up.
Anyone interests in joining should sign up.
questions.explanation: 'Who is interested' se reduce a 'interested' (participio pasado con valor de adjetivo). Cuidado clásico: 'interested' (siento interés) vs 'interesting' (soy interesante) — se confunden por calco del español. Regla: -ed describe la EMOCIÓN sentida; -ing describe la CAUSA de la emoción.
examples: Anyone concerned about the recent policy changes should attend Friday's town hall.
Anyone worried about the exam can book a one-on-one with the tutor. → cartel académico

questions.statement: Las cláusulas relativas reducidas son más comunes en escritura formal que en habla casual.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Producen frases más densas, compactas y elegantes — típicas de textos legales, académicos, periodísticos y corporativos. En habla espontánea, los nativos prefieren las relativas completas ('the report that they submitted'). Usar reducciones en conversación casual puede sonar libresco o afectado.
examples: Formal: The report submitted yesterday needs urgent revision. → email corporativo
Casual: The report that they submitted yesterday needs some serious revision, honestly.

questions.text: The passengers travelling with young children may board the aircraft first.
questions.explanation: Frase clásica de megafonía de aeropuerto y aviación. 'Travelling with young children' = 'who are travelling'. Prosodia neutra, ritmo pausado y clara articulación (los anuncios se diseñan para máxima inteligibilidad). Connected speech: 'travelling with' se enlaza suave, y 'young children' recibe énfasis informativo.
examples: Guests staying more than one night automatically receive complimentary breakfast.
Passengers requiring special assistance should notify a member of the cabin crew.

questions.prompt: Un artículo de HR analiza el trabajo remoto.
questions.question: Choose the correct reduction of: 'The employees who work from home have higher productivity.'
options: The employees worked from home have higher productivity.
The employees to work from home have higher productivity.
The employees working from home have higher productivity.
The employees work from home have higher productivity.
questions.explanation: 'Who work' (presente simple habitual/continuo) se convierte en 'working' (activo). Los empleados HACEN la acción de trabajar, así que va -ing, no PP. La opción A ('worked') sería pasado o pasivo, ambos incorrectos aquí.
examples: The people living in this neighbourhood are honestly the friendliest I've ever met.
Students studying medicine typically work exhausting hours during their residencies.

questions.target: The building designed by that famous architect has become a landmark of the city.
questions.explanation: Reducción con participio pasado pasivo. Estructura estándar en descripciones de arquitectura, arte, patrimonio, guías turísticas y críticas culturales. Prosodia: pausa suave tras 'architect' y énfasis emocional en 'landmark'. Nativos añaden precisión: 'iconic', 'controversial', 'award-winning' antes del sustantivo.
examples: The novel written by her older sister became an unexpected international bestseller.
The film directed by Nolan won several BAFTAs and cemented his reputation.

questions.prompt: Identifica el uso de -ing con valor activo continuo abstracto.
questions.question: Which sentence uses a reduced clause meaning 'that face(s)' (active continuous)?
options: The problems facing us are enormous.
The problems solved by the team are complex.
The problems considered in the report vary widely.
The problems being discussed today are urgent.
questions.explanation: 'Facing us' = 'that face us / that are facing us'. Aquí el -ing tiene sentido activo continuo con matiz de estado presente (los problemas nos afrontan). Es un patrón muy común en discurso político y periodístico serio ('the challenges facing our generation...', 'the issues facing the industry...').
examples: The challenges facing our generation are truly unprecedented in modern history. → editorial
The dangers lurking in unregulated markets are real, and we should not ignore them.
